- When sentiment is negative for 2+ consecutive days, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If model forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10% below peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 5–7 days after a sharp rise, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average.  
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope and shift mean toward prior 10-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome drops below 70% of 14-day moving average, apply downward bias of 3–5% to next 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 patterns, model should not overreact to single-day sentiment shifts; use 3-day rolling average for smoothing.
